texts.preamble: Da vs Ravi Raheja on 9 August, 2018 In The Court Of Samar Vishal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Ii, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 39078/2016 Date of Institution : 04.06.2008 Date of reserving judgement : 09.08.2018 Date of pronouncement : 09.08.2018 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus Sh. Ravi Raheja S/o Late Sh. Manohar Lal Raheja M/s Raheja Sweets, Shop No. 5, Hanuman Mandir, K.M. texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of th e PFA Act and Rules. DA vs Ravi Raheja 2. As per the complaint, on 08.01.2018 at about 5.00 pm food inspector Gian Chand purchased a sample of "Laddoo" an article of food for analysis from accused Ravi Raheja from the premises of M/s Raheja Sweets, Shop No. 5, Hanuman Mandir, K.M. College, Delhi University, Delhi - 110007 where the said article was found stored for sale and he was found conducting the business and vending the same for human consumption at the time of taking the sample. The sample consisted of 1500 gms of "Laddoo" (ready for sale) taken from an open tray bearing no label declaration. The Da vs Ravi Raheja on 9 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136403627/ 1 sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh. Yogesh Partap, SDM/LHA. The sample was taken after the laddoo broken into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean & dry knife over clean and dry tray and mixed them properly with the help of same knife. The sample was divided into three parts then and there by putting in three clean and dry bottles. 40 drops of formaline added in each sample counterpart of the sample bottles. Each bottles containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the bottle containing the sample. Notice in Form-VI was given to accused Ravi Raheja and the price of sample was also paid to him vide vendor receipt dated 08.01.2008. Panchnama too were prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by the Food Inspector were signed by accused Ravi Raheja and by the other witness Sh. J.P. Bhardwaj, FA. Before taking the sample efforts were made to get the public witnesses to join the proceedings but none came forward, as such Sh. J.P. DA vs Ravi Raheja Bhardwaj, FA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA Code Number 41/LHA/20739 in intact condition alongwith copy of memo in Form VII and another copy of memo in Form VII under seal cover were sent separately to the Public Analyst, Delhi and two parts of the sample alongwith two copies of memos in Form VII were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact conditions. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be non-conforming to the standard under the PFA Act and Rules. The report of Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample is adulterated because total dye content of the synthetic colour used exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 100 ppm." 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused Ravi Raheja was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Raheja Sweets, Shop No. 5, Hanuman Mandir, K.M. College, Delhi University, Delhi - 110007, at the time of taking sample and he looks after its day to day business and as such he is incharge of and responsible for the conduct of the said shop. 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 04.06.2008 alleging violation of Section 2 (ia)(a)(j)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954 and Rule 30 read with Rule 28 and Rule 29 of PFA Rules 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(A) of PFA Act against the accused. DA vs Ravi Raheja 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 27.01.2011. The accused has exercised his right of getting the sample analysed from CFL. According to CFL report the sample does not confirm to standard because the the synthetic colour was 236.396 which has to be not more than 100 ppm. Based on pre-charge evidence as well as the CFL report, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(A) PFA Act being violation of Section 2 (ia)(a)(j)&(m) of PFA Act, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Da vs Ravi Raheja on 9 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136403627/ 2 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined two witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Gian Chand, PW-2 FI D.V. Singh, PW-3 SDM/LHA Yogesh Pratap and PW-4 FA J.P. Bhardwaj. PW-1 and PW-4 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. Yogesh Pratap. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 gms Laddu lying in an open tray bearing no label declaration, breaking it into smallest possible pieces, dividing it in three parts and putting in clean and dry bottles, adding 40 drops of formaline in each bottle as preservative, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice Ex.PW-1/B, DA vs Ravi Raheja Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C, Report under Rule 9(e) Ex.PW-3/A. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample alongwith copy of memo in Form VII were deposited to PA on 09.01.2008 vide PA receipt Ex.PW1/D and remaining two counterparts alongwth two copies of memo VII were sent to LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex.PW1/E. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/F was received according to which the sample was adulterated and on the directions of SDM/LHA, PW-1 started the investigations. During investigations, PW-1 sent a letter Ex. PW1/G to vendor and received reply Ex.PW1/G1 stating that the said shop is not registered with the Sales Tax or MCD. PW-1 also sent letter Ex.PW1/H to Vat Officer Ward No. 68. After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-2/A was taken from the Director PFA and the complaint Ex.PW-2/B was filed in the Court. A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex.PW-2/C was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex.PW2/D. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the sampling method was not proper or that the accused had been falsely implicated. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 26.08.2016 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. The accused has not led any defence evidence and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein Da vs Ravi Raheja on 9 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136403627/ 3 are concerned. 13. In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed as under:- (a) The accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt if on account of delay or lapse on the part of prosecution to institute a prosecution, the Director CFL is unable to analyse the sample because of delay or of the sample undergoes a change for this reason. ( b) Once the Director has examined the sample and has delivered his certificate, under proviso to sub-section (5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate is final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein. In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing that the said ruling has been constantly followed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in many other decisions. Da vs Ravi Raheja on 9 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136403627/ 4 16. This issue of variation was considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Delhi Administration vs Vidya Gupta Criminal Appeal No. 625 of 2018 dated 24.04.2018 wherein it was held that the finding of Hon'ble High Court in Kanshi Nath vs State and State vs Mahender Kumar & Ors, which hold that if in the comparison of reports of PA and the Director vast variations are found, then the samples are not representative, is improper. Those decisions do not lay down good law.
